transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My husband told me I had to come. Him and... well, the people down at the warehouse, they keep acting like I'm crazy. But I'm not. I just... I know they've been watching my moves. They keep changing my pallet counts on purpose so I don't get that supervisor spot. But... yeah. I guess that's why I'm here.
Do you really believe that the people at the warehouse are intentionally changing your pallet counts?

Yeah. I mean... I just said that. I wouldn't say it if it wasn't true. I know how to count my own pallets. I do my work, and then the numbers get changed. They're watching me. They just don't want me getting that supervisor job, so they mess with it. I don't know why everyone acts like I'm making it up.
Do you think anyone else is involved in this, or is it just the people at the warehouse?

I don't know. Just them, I guess. My husband... he just thinks I'm crazy. But it's the warehouse people watching me. They're the ones changing the counts so I don't get the spot. I already told you that.
Do you think this is all part of a larger plan against you?
I don't know about a larger plan. I just know what they're doing. They're watching me and changing the counts. That's it. I already said that.
Do you still believe the people at the warehouse are watching you and changing your pallet counts?

Yeah. I do. I mean... I'm only here because my husband made me come. Him and the people at work, they act like I'm losing my mind. But... I know what I see. They're watching everything I do. They change the numbers so I don't get the supervisor spot. I know they do.
Do you think there's any way to convince you that the people at the warehouse are not watching you and changing your pallet counts?

No. I mean... you can't convince me when I already know what's happening. Like I said, I only came in because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I'm crazy. But I'm not. I know they've been watching my moves and changing the pallet counts to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. So... no.
Have you ever had any thoughts or beliefs that you later found out were not true?
No. I don't think so.
Do you think it's possible that you might be mistaken about the warehouse people watching you?

No. I'm not mistaken. I... I already told you, they're watching me. They change the numbers. My husband thinks I'm crazy, they all do, but... I know what I'm seeing. They just don't want me to get that supervisor job.
Do you think there's anything that could happen that would change your mind about the warehouse people watching you?

I just... I don't know why we keep going over this. No. 

Like I already said, I only came in because my husband and the warehouse guys keep acting like I'm crazy. But I'm not. I know they're watching my moves and changing my pallet counts so I don't get that supervisor spot. So... nothing's going to change my mind.
For how long have you believed that the people at the warehouse are watching you and changing your pallet counts?
It's been... about eight months. That's how long they've been watching me and changing things. And... when the voices started, too. Just about eight months now.
What do you mean by 'when the voices started'?

Just... what I said. I hear a voice sometimes. 

It's... it's a man's voice. I'll be in the aisle at work, or just at home folding clothes, and I hear him clear as day. He tells me... he says, "Nicole, check it again." Even when nobody is anywhere near me. 

I don't really like talking about it. That's all it is.
Is the voice you hear only telling you to check things again or does it say other things as well?

I... I just told you. It's really just what I said. He just tells me to check it again, like when I'm at work or... doing my laundry. 

I don't really listen for anything else. I told you I don't like talking about it.
Does the voice ever tell you to do something other than checking things again?
No. Just... no. Like I said, it's just about checking the pallets or... whatever I'm doing. It doesn't say anything else. I really don't want to keep talking about him.
Does the voice ever tell you to do something that you feel you must do?
No. It's not like that. I don't... I don't feel like I have to do it. I just... I already told you everything he says. I really don't want to talk about this anymore.
Does the voice ever tell you to do something that you think you should do?
No. I don't... I don't know. I don't think about it like that. Look, I just told you I'm done talking about him. Can we please just talk about something else?
Does the voice ever tell you to do something that you feel like you cannot ignore?
No. I... look, I already answered this. I just told you I'm done talking about him. I'm not answering any more questions about it.
Do you think other people at the warehouse, who are not involved in changing your pallet counts, also believe that those specific people are watching you?

No. They... they all act like I'm crazy. That's why I'm even here, because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like it's all in my head. But I know they're watching my moves. I know they're changing the pallet counts so I don't get that supervisor spot. The others just... they don't see it.
Do you think the voice you hear is related to the people at the warehouse who you believe are watching you?

I don't... I don't know if they're connected. I just... sometimes I'm in the aisle at work, or even just at home folding clothes, and I hear this man's voice. It's clear as day. He just says, "Nicole, check it again." And there's nobody around. I don't know if it's them. I just hear it.
Is there anything that could happen that would make you question whether the voice you hear is real?
I don't... no. I don't know what you mean by that. I hear him. So... I don't know why I would question it.
Do you find it difficult to express your thoughts in a way that others can understand?

I guess. People tell me that. When I try to explain what's going on... they say they can't follow me. Like, my words just run from the forklift sheets, to the church signs... to my husband's tone of voice. I don't know. They just say they don't get what I'm saying.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent delusions of persecution, as evidenced by her belief that her coworkers are watching her and changing her pallet counts to prevent her from getting a supervisor spot. She also experiences auditory hallucinations, hearing a voice that tells her to 'check it again'. These symptoms have been present for approximately eight months, indicating a chronic course. The patient's delusions and hallucinations are not better explained by any other condition, and she shows significant impairment in social and occupational functioning due to these symptoms.
